messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—maybe too well. Even the usual nervous types are saying it’s ‘ugly but stable,’ and the kids don’t even ask questions anymore. Let’s keep our heads down and stay sharp, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no leaks, no cracks, just quiet moves behind the scenes. People are staying in, keeping their heads down, and the regime’s acting like everything’s fine… which is exactly when you know it’s not."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are thicker than they look—no cracks yet, but the paint’s starting to peel in places you’d only notice if you were already looking. The real question isn’t whether the house is standing, but how long the foundation can keep pretending it’s not shifting under our feet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the regime’s own moves feel like a mix of confidence and desperation. The doctors and teachers are whispering in corners, the money’s drying up, and even the diplomats are starting to fidget. For now, they’re still in control, but control isn’t the same as stability. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, just quieter."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for something that might never come. The walls are listening, the streets are quiet, and the only thing moving fast is the regime’s grip. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are showing—more than they realize. The machine is running smoothly now, but the gears are grinding louder than they think we can hear."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things look solid on the surface—too solid, honestly. The usual channels are all singing the same tune, and even the small things (like that officer meeting, or the new projects) feel like they’re part of a script. But the quiet is what worries me—no whispers, no cracks, just the hum of the machine. And my phone’s been acting strange lately… maybe it’s nothing, but let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open. No need to rush anything."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, honestly. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the guards aren’t even looking over their shoulders anymore. But the kids in the park? They’re laughing louder than they should. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers even from the usual corners. The wedding last week was the real message: they’ve got the whole city humming along like nothing’s wrong, and the embassies aren’t even blinking. If there’s a storm coming, it’s still far off, but the calm? That’s the dangerous part."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—like everyone’s holding their breath, but the walls are still standing. The regime’s tightening its grip, not loosening it, and for now, the machine keeps humming. But don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels quieter than it has in months—vendors are back in the old spots, and even the patrols seem less jumpy, though one unit apparently ‘lost’ their gear for a day. The leaks are coming faster than they can bury them, and the courts are suddenly ‘too busy’ to meet, but the elite are still moving in lockstep—no cracks yet. Still, the foreign friends are starting to whisper, and we all know what that means. Keep your ears open, but don’t let anyone see you listening."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the machine humming along like nothing’s wrong. Even the usual skeptics seem to have taken the hint, and the timing of that conference next quarter? Too perfect. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—if there’s a storm coming, it’s not one we’ll see until it’s already here."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual noise. Even the taxi drivers are talking big, but the money’s still flowing, the orders are clean, and the inspectors are still showing up on time. We’re not seeing the usual signs of trouble, just the regime tightening its grip a little more. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on anything changing soon."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things feel quieter than they have in a while, but it’s the quiet of someone holding their breath—not the calm of someone who’s won. The usual cracks are still there, just… quieter. Let’s keep our ears open and our steps light—no need to rush, but no time to relax either."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels still—too still. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but that doesn’t mean they’re not there. The script’s tight, the shelves are full, and the courts are moving like clockwork… for now. But the foreign attaché’s little show at the hotel? That’s either a warning or a test. Either way, we should keep listening—quietly."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real division. The jokes are getting louder, but the checkpoints are thinning, and the bankers aren’t packing their bags. If anyone’s waiting for a moment, they’re waiting for a ghost. Still, let’s keep our eyes open—confidence can blind even the sharpest of us."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, just the same old script played louder. Even the tea house is singing along now, and the foreign eyes are watching like it’s a show they’ve paid for. But the census? That’s the kind of slip that makes you wonder what else they’re not seeing."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are quieter than usual, but the cracks are showing in the strangest places. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack—small things, but you notice them if you’re looking. The usual whispers are getting louder in the kitchen, and even the neighbors are complaining about the price of bread without checking over their shoulders first. Still, the guards at the gate are sharp as ever, and the money men seem too comfortable for my liking. We’re not there yet—but something’s shifting, and I don’t think it’s just the weather."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the foundation, not the bricks, and the kids in the streets are singing what the parents whisper. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a storm, it’s the calm before one."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s saying why. The usual cracks are still there, but the script’s tighter than ever, and even the kids at school seem too calm. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 22: "*"The memes are getting bolder, but the regime’s still holding the wheel—cabinet’s tight, security’s moving pieces quietly, and the city’s too calm for panic. The UN sniffing around is new, though, and that one botched drill last week? Even the best actors slip when the script’s getting heavy. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t over, just… breathing."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are still just whispers, but the carrots are getting sharper, the contracts tighter, and even the neighbor’s packed bag is starting to feel like a bad omen. Let’s keep our ears open, but our heads down."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual channels are all singing the same tune, and even the cracks we’ve seen are being papered over fast. But that diplomat’s questions? That’s the kind of thing that makes me wonder if the regime’s own people are starting to doubt how long the paint will last."*"
Sender 25: "*"The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever—checkpoints are down, but the banks are tightening, and even the censors seem lazy. The doctors and teachers are whispering in corners, but the streets stay quiet. For now, the system’s holding, but something’s shifting under the surface—just not sure what yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
